chapter: Will Marion Cook and the Southern Syncopated Orchestra
title: Voyage to Liverpool and bodies in the Mersey
summary: They sailed on 1 May 1919 on the Nordland and on arrival saw Black bodies in the Mersey, victims of race riots after soldiers found their wives with African workers; they were escorted by police.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Let me get this straight, here. What were the dates. When did you first go over there?
I should have told you. We landed in Liverpool, on the 1st, on the 10th of May. We left the United States, New York on the 1st of May.
1919. And arrived in Liverpool on a German passenger ship that was taken by Allies during the war, named the Nordland.
And we arrived in Liverpool -- I'm going to skip certain things. Liverpool was not very interesting.
We arrived in Liverpool. We took this train. I'll tell you after if you think
Briggs
it's necessary to put it in.
Well, why don't you put it in, and then you can cut it from the transcript later --
Well, we arrived and taxied up in the estuary for the Mercy River some of the groups, found some curious looking objects in the river, you see.

And as we taxied further on to the pier, they realized that they were bodies. And Mr. Latimore and Mr. Cook tried to find out what's the matter, and after careful attention they saw they were black bodies floating in the river.
And so they -- Cook, Latimore, went to the Captain and tried to find out. He was aware, you know. He told him what had happened were race riots with the soldiers coming in from France.
And finding their wives, in the company of what you call natives who were sent
Briggs

to England to work in the factories while other men were overseas in France. And they had not only taken their wives, but they left offspring. That was pretty bad, you see. And the men, you know, you can imagine a soldier coming over and -- well, what you don't know won't worry you -- but then you see something that shouldn't be, that's a different thing, and they'd taken the law into their own hands. And every colored person in this -- there were six bodies floating.
So these were, what, Africans.
Africans, yes. Most were Africans.
And they brought them in to work in factories.
Into factories, when the other men were -- yes. And, apparently, we learned after that the poor guys that were assassinated were
Briggs
Sure, that's usually what happens.
But we didn't have any difficulty. We had a police escort take us to the railroad station.
So you went right -- they got the police down.
We had a police escort.to the station, right. And nothing happened.
